input: Shadow a colleague in a different department

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is a single observation session or a multi-day, multi-task immersion changes how the plan is structured and how much time needs to be blocked.
Whether the user already has a specific colleague in mind or needs to identify and approach someone determines whether the first step is outreach or logistics.
The department being shadowed shapes what activities to observe, what prep to do, and what questions to prepare in advance.
The available time window and any workplace approval processes (e.g. manager sign-off, formal job-shadow programme) set hard limits on scheduling and process steps.
Understanding the user's goal — career exploration, cross-team empathy, skill acquisition, networking — determines what to prioritise during the shadow and how to measure a good outcome.
Whether the shadowing will be in-person, remote, or hybrid affects how to set it up, what tools are needed, and what the experience will actually look like.
How the user wants to document or follow up — notes, a reflection write-up, a follow-on meeting — determines what outputs to plan for and how to make the learning stick.

gold.taskTitle: Shadow a colleague in a different department
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange and carry out a job-shadowing experience with a colleague from another department in their organisation.

questions.title: How long should the shadowing experience last?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a single session (e.g. a few hours), a full day, or spread across multiple days — this determines the overall scope and structure of the plan.

questions.title: Do you already have a specific colleague in mind?
questions.description: Establish whether the user needs to identify and approach someone, or whether a person is already lined up, so the first action step can be set correctly.

questions.title: Which department do you want to shadow?
questions.description: Knowing the target department helps tailor the preparation — relevant background reading, questions to ask, and activities likely to be observed.

questions.title: Does your workplace require manager or HR approval first?
questions.description: Determine whether there are formal sign-off steps or an existing job-shadow programme to follow, which sets hard constraints on the process and timeline.

questions.title: What is the main reason you want to do this?
questions.description: Understanding the underlying goal — career exploration, building cross-team empathy, learning a specific skill, or networking — shapes what to focus on during the shadow.

questions.title: Will the shadowing be in-person, remote, or hybrid?
questions.description: The format affects how the session is arranged, what tools or access are needed, and what the day-of experience will look like.

questions.title: How do you want to capture and follow up on what you learn?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user plans to take notes, write a reflection, share insights with their manager, or schedule a follow-on conversation — this determines what outputs to build into the plan.
